headline: Ep 14 posted the channel's best first-30-seconds (88% at 0:32) and its worst first-ten-minutes: 26% at 1:05, 11% at the 10% mark, and vs_typical 0.03–0.06 across the 10-minute Astra marquee (1:22–11:33) before the perp finally started — then the tail is the strongest ever recorded (vs_typical 0.89 at 'Gavin trades Bitcoin' 32:36, 0.61–0.67 through Liquid and the perp check, flat 5.3% to the end card). The no-title-card experiment did not move the 1:05 cliff (Ep 14 26% vs Ep 13 38%, Ep 12 27%, Ep 11 30%): the seam is cold-open → welcome, card or no card. Avg view % 7.1 is the lowest long-form since Ep 3; launch CTR 1.83% on 1,531 impressions is down from Ep 13's 2.46% / Ep 12's 2.01%; +2 subs is the most any episode has earned since June. Shorts: the Sep 5–11 week hit 2,697 views (best ever, spaghetti 977 + Fable 1,168) and the Ep 14 batch produced the first browse-distributed hit — 'We gave a fruit fly brain $100 to trade Bitcoin' 272 views from 821 impressions at 8.4% CTR and 85.7% AVD — while the two provocation picks split ("Astra is my top guy" 232 via shorts feed; 'MCPs were a waste of time' 58). Subs 24 → 26, zero lost in 9 days. Ep 15 went live 9/18 06:51 UTC as 'They Found an Infinite Money Glitch at a Bank' with the perp at 1:22 and the reveal at 3:53 — the first episode built the way the last three weeks of notes asked — but it launched with 0 tags and no caption track because the force-ssl token was revoked by the manual upload; re-auth and patch both today, inside the 7-day impressions window.

production.evidence: yt_fetch 9/19: -DEI0oQM2Ys 'They Found an Infinite Money Glitch at a Bank', publishedAt 2026-09-18T06:51Z, tags []. yt_captions.py hung on the OAuth browser flow (token_captions.json last refreshed 9/11; Jackson's Studio uploads have revoked tokens 7/18, 7/20, 7/31, 8/20, 9/4). production.title: No-title-card experiment: FAILED to move the 1:05 cliff — the leak is the cold-open → welcome seam itself
production.evidence: Retention at 0:32 / 1:05 / 1:37: Ep 14 (no card) 88% / 26% / 19%; Ep 13 (card at :56) 84% / 38% / 26%; Ep 12 (card) 74% / 27% / 22%; Ep 11 (card) 81% / 30% / 24%. Ep 14's cold open held better than any episode and then lost 62 points in the 33 s that contain the 0:44 welcome seam — more than the three carded episodes lost across the same span. Ep 14 avg view % 7.1 (Ep 13 8.99, Ep 12 7.3, Ep 11 18.1).
production.recommendation: Stop treating the card as the variable. The viewer who leaves at 0:44–1:05 is leaving because the show switches from 'best moment' to 'hello'. Ep 15 tests the alternative structure (welcome 0:40–1:22, perp at 1:22, board reveal at 3:53): grade its 1:05 and 10% marks next week before changing anything else. Keep no-card as the house style meanwhile (it costs nothing and reads cleaner).
production.status_note: closed 9/19: experiment run on Ep 14, result negative; lesson moved to the recording item on the first payoff.

production.title: Ep 14 shorts: the fruit-fly short is the first BROWSE-distributed hit (8.4% CTR on 821 impressions) — replicate the shape
production.evidence: Ep 14 batch (5 live of 8): fruit fly $100 to trade Bitcoin 272 views / 821 imp / 8.4% CTR / 85.7% AVD; "Astra is my top guy" 232 views from 10 impressions (pure shorts-feed swipe); Wikipedia squatting 60 / 134 imp; MCPs waste of time 58 / 83 imp; goblin mode 35 / 51 imp. Prior 4-digit shorts got their views from the feed (Fable programmer 1,168 views on 50 impressions; spaghetti 977 on 549 imp at 1.64%). 8.4% is 3–5× any short with >100 impressions on the channel. Class ledger for the [prod] pick experiment: 2 provocation → 232 + 58; 1 physical/animal+money → 272; 2 premise/explainer → 60 + 35.
production.recommendation: The fruit-fly short is the template for a browse-surface short: a concrete absurd premise with money in it (an animal brain, $100, Bitcoin) and a face reacting in the first frame. Ep 15 bench candidates in that shape: '25× long the yen, R-E-K-T' with the board on screen, 'Wintermute printed infinite money at a bank', 'I let Facebook buy my shoes'. Keep one provocation per batch (they swipe-perform), drop the explainer class (Wikipedia/goblin both bottom-half two batches running).
production.status_note: pick-class experiment logged for Ep 14; 3 of 8 shorts still scheduled (9/18–9/20), regrade next pull.

production.title: Comment-reply test: SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS 5 → 6 lifetime after +1,340 more shorts views — fail; retire the metric as a task
production.evidence: Traffic-source deltas 9/9 → 9/18: SHORTS +1,340 views, YT_SEARCH +422 (largest search week ever; 1,030 lifetime), SUBSCRIBER +163, YT_OTHER_PAGE +50, RELATED_VIDEO +26, SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS +1. The Fable short now shows 2 comments (was 4 on 9/9) — the API can't tell whether that's replies-as-threads, deletions, or spam filtering, so the 'reply' arm of the test is unverifiable from here. The pass bar was ≥10 by 9/23; at 6 with 4 days left and a +1/1,340 rate, it will not clear.
production.recommendation: Close it. Shorts-feed viewers do not take the related-video link at any rate we can move; the funnel evidence that IS moving is YT_SEARCH (+422 in 9 days, most of it long-form titles with 'AGI' in them) and SUBSCRIBER (+163 views, +74 min). Keep the branded ender and pinned comment as the funnel path and stop reporting SHORTS_CONTENT_LINKS as an open item.
production.status_note: closed 9/19 by the experiment's own criterion (≥10 not reachable).

production.title: Subs 24 → 26 with zero lost in 9 days; the LIKE+SUBSCRIBE overlay's 2-episode sample is weakly positive
production.evidence: Daily 9/9–9/15: +1 (9/12), +1 (9/14), 0 lost — first stretch since July with no unsubscribes. Long-form subs_gained: Ep 14 +2 (212 views, 0.94%), Ep 13 +1 (236, 0.42%), Ep 12 0 (299) — the overlay shipped in Ep 13. Shorts since 9/9: 0 subs from ~1,340 views (0.0%). Channel total 26.
production.recommendation: Keep the overlay (Ep 15 has it at 5:47 and 27:45). Long-form is now the only sub source on the channel: 3 of the last 3 subs came from episode pages. That argues for the Ep 15 structure (payoff early) more than for any shorts change.
production.status_note: 2-episode sample: +3 subs vs 0 on the prior episode; not significant, but directionally right. Regrade after Ep 15.

recording.title: Ep 14 spent 10 minutes on the marquee before the perp — vs_typical 0.03–0.06 the whole way, the worst stretch ever recorded; Ep 15 is the corrected structure
recording.evidence: Ep 14 chapters vs retention: welcome 0:44 (88% → 26% by 1:05), Astra marquee 1:22–11:33 at 19% → 5.3% with vs_typical 0.061 (1:22), 0.029 (5:22), 0.030 (7:48), 0.040 (8:58); perp reveal 11:33 at 5.3%. From there the curve is FLAT at 5.3% for 42 minutes and vs_typical climbs: 0.25 (Navier-Stokes 15:47), 0.49 (check-in 25:45, fruit fly 27:31), 0.89 at 'Gavin trades Bitcoin' 32:36 — the highest vs_typical point on any episode — 0.67 perp check, 0.61 Liquid, 0.46 wrap. The [rec] experiment ('perp reveal inside 90 s of the segment start; check-in after the first payoff') was not run: the perp segment itself started at 11:33. Ep 13 (perp at 2:37) held 19% at the 10% mark; Ep 14 held 11%; Ep 12 (3-min tangent) 8%.
recording.recommendation: Ep 15 does it right on tape — perp at 1:22, board at 3:53, marquee at 5:20 — so the next pull is the test, not another instruction. If Ep 15's 10% mark clears 20% (target from 9/9), lock the order: welcome ≤45 s → perp reveal → marquee. If it doesn't, the problem is the welcome seam itself and the next experiment is opening cold on the perp board with no welcome at all.

recording.title: The back half is where the show is best — every host-with-a-thing segment beat every analysis segment again
recording.evidence: Ep 14 vs_typical by segment: Gavin the fruit fly 0.50–0.89, perp check 0.67, Liquid explainer 0.61 (the best a pure explainer has scored; it had a heist and a number in it), the white-hat-fee/FBI debate 0.40, wrap 0.46. Astra marquee 0.03–0.06, Navier-Stokes 0.25. Ep 13's pattern was identical (sycophancy stories 0.64, Astra-vs-GLM 0.20). Three episodes running, the AI-industry-state segment is the retention floor and it is always placed first.
recording.recommendation: Either lead with the segment that has a creature, a victim, or a number on screen, or cut the industry-state block to ≤5 min and put it after the first payoff. Ep 15's marquee (pace the frontier) runs 5:20–18:43, 13 minutes: watch its vs_typical next week; if it repeats 0.05, the standing rule becomes 'no industry-state segment before minute 20'.

recording.title: Cold opens are solved — 88% / 84% / 81% at 0:32 the last three episodes; the finale tease keeps working
recording.evidence: Ep 14's five-beat 44 s cold open held 88% at 0:32, the channel's best; Ep 13's finale-tease open 84%; Ep 11 81%; Ep 12 (no tease) 74%. None of the loss in any of these episodes happens before the welcome.
recording.recommendation: Keep the recipe (3–5 beats, ≤45 s, one beat teases the ending). Spend the next change on what follows it, not on the open.

recording.title: Provocation still drives the swipe feed, but the browse surface wants a physical premise with money in it
recording.evidence: Since 9/9: 'Astra is my top guy' 232 views (provocation, feed-distributed: 10 impressions); 'MCPs were a waste of time (I built one)' 58 — same class, didn't travel. Fruit fly $100 → 272 views from 821 browse impressions at 8.4% CTR. Fable-programmer short (1,168) picked up 0 new comments this week. Ep 14 recorded several browse-shaped moments on tape (Gavin trades Bitcoin, the $100, 'Bitcoin is a stablecoin') and one landed.
recording.recommendation: On mic, once per episode, do a bit with a prop, an animal, or a live dollar figure on screen — those are the only shorts YouTube has ever pushed to browse for this channel. Keep the one arguable claim per segment for the feed.

recording.title: Perp-rides-all-episode keeps holding the ending — Ep 14's tail was dead flat at 5.3% for 42 minutes
recording.evidence: Ep 14 retention from 11:33 to 54:11 never drops below 5.3%; the two perp-board checks (12:16, 34:16) and the Gavin-trades-Bitcoin insert sit at vs_typical 0.67–0.89. Ep 13 and Ep 12 tails were flat at 5–6% the same way.
recording.recommendation: Keep it structural. Ep 15 rides the board from 22:30 to the end and closes on the −$13 → −$11 recovery; no change.
